Edit maps

Source: R/map.R
map.Rd

A map holds values under string keys. When replicas set the same key concurrently, one write wins on every replica.

  • map_set() stores plain values, given as key = value arguments.

  • map_set_container() stores a new, empty child container under key and returns its handle.

  • map_get() returns the value under key, a handle if it is a container, or NULL if the key is absent.

  • map_has() reports whether each of keys is present.

  • map_ensure_container() returns the child container under key, creating it if the key is empty. Unlike map_set_container(), which always makes a fresh container, the container it creates is shared: replicas that each create it independently end up editing the same one, with all their edits merged. Use it for containers that are created lazily on first use. It is an error if key already holds a plain value, a container of another type, or a container made by map_set_container().

  • map_delete() removes the keys named in ..., as in map_delete(map, "a", "b") or map_delete(map, keys), and map_clear() removes every key.

  • map_last_editor() returns the peer id of the replica that last wrote key, or NA if the key has never been written.

  • map_keys() returns the keys in sorted order, and map_length() the number of entries.

A map handle also works with the base functions an R user would reach for with a named list: map$key and map[[key]] read like map_get(), map$key = value and map[[key]] = value write one key like map_set(), names() is map_keys(), length() is map_length(), and as.list() is container_value(). As with a list, assigning NULL removes the key: map$key = NULL is map_delete(map, "key"). To store a null, use map_set(map, key = NULL). Assignments can reach through child containers, as in map$child$key = value.

Loro allows the empty string as a key, and a document written by another Loro client may contain one. It is supported only for compatibility with such documents: it can be read and removed like any other key, but R does not allow an empty argument name, so it cannot be written with map_set(). Use map[[""]] = value if one has to be changed.

Usage

map_set(map, ...)

map_set_container(map, key, type)

map_ensure_container(map, key, type)

map_get(map, key)

map_has(map, keys)

map_delete(map, ...)

map_clear(map)

map_keys(map)

map_length(map)

map_last_editor(map, key)

Arguments

map

A map handle, from doc_map() or a parent container. A loro_doc is also accepted and stands for its default root container; see doc_text().

...

Values to store, each named with its key, for example map_set(map, title = "Notes", done = FALSE); see the Values section. These are dynamic dots, so a named list can be spliced in with !!! and a key held in a variable can be used with "{key}" := value. Values are stored in order, so if one is rejected the ones before it stay set. For map_delete(), the keys to remove, as strings or character vectors.

key

A string.

type

Type of the child container: "text", "map", "list", "movable_list", "counter", or "tree".

keys

A character vector of keys.

Value

map_set(), map_delete(), and map_clear() return map invisibly. map_set_container() and map_ensure_container() return a container handle, and map_last_editor() a string. map_get() returns a value or handle, map_has() a logical vector, map_keys() a character vector, and map_length() an integer.

Values

Plain values are converted as follows. NULL and NA become null. Length-one logical, numeric, and character vectors become scalars; other unnamed vectors and unnamed lists become lists; named vectors and named lists become maps. Raw vectors are stored as binary, and any names on them are dropped. Objects with a class attribute (factors, dates, data frames) are rejected, and other attributes such as dim are ignored.

Strings are stored as UTF-8. Strings in another encoding are converted, and strings that are not valid text are rejected. Values may be nested up to 1000 levels deep.

An empty vector or list is always stored as an empty list, even if it carries a names attribute, so an empty map cannot be written as a plain value.

A plain value is stored as a single unit: concurrent changes replace it whole. To let replicas merge edits inside a value, store a child container instead. Values read back as scalars and (possibly nested) lists; map entries are returned sorted by key, comparing the keys byte by byte (as sort(method = "radix") does), which is not always the order sort() gives in your locale.

Examples

doc = loro_doc()
meta = doc_map(doc, "meta")
map_set(meta, title = "Notes", tags = c("a", "b"))

body = map_set_container(meta, "body", "text")
text_insert(body, 1, "Hello")

map_keys(meta)
#> [1] "body"  "tags"  "title"
map_get(meta, "title")
#> [1] "Notes"
meta$title
#> [1] "Notes"
text_get(meta$body)
#> [1] "Hello"

meta$title = "Shopping"
map_delete(meta, "tags")
as.list(meta)
#> $body
#> [1] "Hello"
#> 
#> $title
#> [1] "Shopping"
#>
